Sometimes you need a flashlight more than a map.

When you're facing an uncertain decision, it's tempting to want the entire path laid out before you begin. But you may only need enough clarity to see the next useful step. The rest can become clearer as you move forward.

The Thinking Lens helps you explore what's in front of you and find a thoughtful next step: https://thethinkinglens.garrettsdevdesk.com

We often want to know how everything will work out before we're willing to begin.

But plans change, people surprise us, and new information appears along the way. Even careful planning can't account for every possibility, especially when the future depends on things outside our control.

Try separating what you can reasonably plan today from what you'll have to learn later. You may discover that fewer questions need immediate answers than you thought.

A flashlight only shows you the next few feet, and sometimes that's exactly enough.

When the entire future feels overwhelming, bring your attention closer. What can you understand today? What decision is actually in front of you? What small action would help you learn more?

The Thinking Lens offers a calmer way to explore those questions: https://thethinkinglens.garrettsdevdesk.com

Some questions can't be answered from where you're standing today.

You might want to know how a project will develop, whether a new direction will work, or what opportunities will appear next year. Some of those answers depend on experiences you haven't had yet.

Try listing the questions weighing on your mind. Mark the ones you can investigate now and the ones that require more time or experience. Give your attention to what you can actually learn.

Step one might change what you need to know about step six.

That's worth remembering when you're trying to plan every detail before starting. A thoughtful first step can reveal new information, change your priorities, or show you an option you hadn't considered. Then you can adjust your plans with a clearer understanding.

Explore your next step with The Thinking Lens: https://thethinkinglens.garrettsdevdesk.com

You don't need the whole road illuminated to take one thoughtful step.

There's value in recognizing what you can see clearly today and accepting that some parts of the journey will become understandable only after you've moved forward. You can make careful decisions without having a complete picture of the future.

When you're facing uncertainty, do you prefer making a detailed plan or taking a small step and adjusting as you learn?
